items.title: Apollo "UAP"s explained
items.content:
Apollo 12 photo AS12–46–6842, which shows a purported “UAP”, can you spot it?

On May 8th, the Department of War released a trove of files showing various images, testimonials, audio recordings, and videos capturing what appear to be unexplainable phenomena.

The most striking images are the ones captured on the lunar surface during the Apollo 12 and Apollo 17 missions, and in particular, one image that shows a “streak” of blue particles above the lunar surface.

On the official DoW site, we are provided with a short description of the image:

“This archival photograph depicts the lunar surface as viewed from the landing site of Apollo 12. This image features a highlighted area of interest slightly to the right of the vertical axis of the frame, above the horizon, in which unidentified phenomena are visible.

This image has been modified from its original state to assist viewers in identifying specific areas of interest. These highlights are provided for contextual purposes only. Such alterations do not constitute an analytical judgment, investigative conclusion, or factual determination regarding the nature or significance of the subject matter.”

And the attached edited image:

Edited Apollo 12 “UAP” image

The image provided is of the JPEG format (with lossy compression, which generates further artifacts) and of a small 2.4MB size. It’s titled nasa-uap-vm1-apollo-12–1969 (which is technically incorrect since “Unidentified Aerial Phenomena” would presumably only be found in the atmosphere… not above the lunar surface).

Looking through the publicly available Apollo 12 images we can see that this image is actually titled AS12–46–6842 (46 stands for the magazine number, and 6842 for the specific captured frame). The website ‘March to the Moon’, which scans the original film rolls stored in the Johnson Space Center, allows us to download the original scanned film at a much higher quality (up to 1.3 GB in TIFF format). You can download it here....

items.title: The salad market mystery
items.content:
It often happens that I desire kale, but I want it to be clean and cut up, and while shops do sell this product by the bucketload, they are actually only willing to sell it by the bucketload. As a normal-sized person wanting a one-off salad, rather than a family of nine celebrating a kale festival, the market seems very uninterested in my existence.

‘Just put it in the fridge and eat it over the coming week, this isn’t a big deal’ I hear someone say. But I already have several plotlines going on in my life. I don’t want an additional kale arc that I need to track to resolution. I don’t want to commit. I just want a no-strings-attached salad that I can consume and walk away from.

‘Just throw out the rest of the kale’, I hear somebody say. But I don’t like throwing out mounds of delicious food that were elaborately grown and brought to me. This might be a moral failing, but so it is—‘salad + perfectly good kale destruction’ is a much less delicious prospect.

The same situation holds for other greens. I love parsley, but I generally want a fistful, not a promise of parsley for the foreseeable future. Basil becomes black and bad if you don’t eat it for too long, but basically the only way to get some basil is to invest in that outcome.

Why can’t I buy greens in convenient units? I’m not the only person who often eats alone, or doesn’t like throwing out food. My dislike of owning a pile of mildly decaying greens and feeling obliged to eat them is stronger than most, but surely not that rare. Greens don’t last well. I would have thought ‘one meal’s worth’ would be the most likely quantity of greens to want, but instead there is no apparent market for that (at least where I am, in California).

What is going on?...

items.title: I'm building redundancies for AI risks. Please join me.
items.content:
Tldr: I'm building an Internet using mesh core or meshtastic. At least, I'm plugging into the already existing ones. But I'm going to be making it so there are no bad spots, and I'm gonna make it so that you can still access Wikipedia and a chat/comms app, even if the Internet goes down.

Also, I'm building off grid  permanent housing. I already bought the solar, batteries, food, wood, everything.

Ok so basically i think AI near term risks are cyber security and bio terrorism. I think someone will jail break a Claude and it'll accidentally take out the cloud. Or parts of it. Or render it unusable for some time. I'm making a secondary Internet, low power, unhackable (or at least harder to hack) low bandwidth. Keeping the necessities of text chat and Wikipedia. But nothing else. I'm running it on meshcore or meshtastic. Probably meshcore. I will be handing out USBs with only text Wikipedia to anyone that needs it. I will be installing repeaters and Wi-Fi bridges powered by solar all over the GTA region. The project is complicated. I can get into it more if you'd like to join me. Basically, there will be servers hosting Wikipedia and chat apps, that are connected to each other over mesh core. Or similar. You'll still be able to text and access Wikipedia as long as you have power on your phone. Also, as long as meshcore is good enough to connect everyone.

Otherwise I'm building off grid for the other risk, bio terrorism. I got everything I mentioned before. And other stuff bandages, compass, binoculars, hunting Gear, farming gear, tools. Everything needed for off grid and other shtf scenarios. No property yet. Can't afford anything in this expensive ass province....

items.title: In Germany someone might have drunk your beer before you
items.content:
Epistemic status: quick research to answer my own curiosity.

AI use: research (reuse process, examples), image attribution, grammar and light phrasing.

While researching Gluten-free water I stumbled upon a story about beer bottle sterilization. This reminded me that in Germany beer bottles are apparently reused, which was surprising to me, so I decided to dig deeper.

In Germany they have separate bins for glass recycling, sorted by the color of the glass.

Photo: Salino01, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 3.0. White, brown and green glass, left to right.

In the image above, the text says that you can throw glass in only between 7am and 8pm. If the container is not yet full, the distance the glass has to fly before hitting something is substantial, so it makes a super loud ding or sometimes even breaks completely.

So at first I assumed that beer bottles from here were reused. Technically they are, but not in the way I thought: they are melted down and remade into new glass.

In Germany there is also Pfand, a deposit you pay for a plastic, metal or glass container when you buy it, so that you are incentivized to return it later.

Photo: Mattes, Wikimedia Commons, public domain. A Tomra reverse vending machine at an Aldi in Munich, 2006. The sign says it takes only Aldi's one-way PET deposit bottles; the display shows 3 bottles, total 0.75 EUR, i.e. 25 cents each.

You get a receipt which you can exchange for money or spend in the store. Sometimes the machine does not accept a perfectly valid bottle and you have to try multiple times in a row.

This is the symbol for the one-way deposit:

Photo: MalteFilmFan, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0....

items.title: Porcus Poem
items.content:
The kids have been excited about Pig Latin a lot lately.  I noticed
that there are a few words that are also English words, or
homophones thereof.  With some help from Claude, especially in
figuring out which words would work well and in checking my work,
here's a poem about a pie and a naughty plover:

I weigh ache bay each pay I pay,

Oh say eats whey, each way ice lei,

Away ate play eye way a prey

I'll weigh eat whey all way a day.

Oh whey, oh neigh! I may I pay!

Away outstay, overplay ate whey

All whey of whey, I may I pay!

Ooh, yay, I slay eat tray outlay!

I weigh, eat whey, all whey, ashtray,

I weigh, underplay, all whey, eyes pay!

Eat sway, eat stray, I weigh eat whey!

Oh say, Old Bay? Owe whey, I may!

I weigh Amway oh say outstay!

I weigh I flay? Oh neigh, away!

I weigh a stay, I weigh I lay,

I weigh owes day all whey a day!

reveal English...

I bake peach pie

So sweet each slice

A plate I pray

I'll eat all day.

Oh, no! My pie!

A stout plover ate

All of my pie!

You sly treat lout!

I eat all trash,

I plunder all pies!

Sweet treats I eat!

So bold? Oh my!

I am so stout!

Why fly? No way!

I stay, I lie,

I doze all day.

Note that this doesn't quite work in my dialect, since "way" and
"whey" are not homophones, but since it works for almost all of my
readers I liked it better with "whey".
